description:
Type de projet: Site web
Objectif: Vendre des abonnements IPTV.

Fonctionnalités clés:
- Système de paiement en ligne.
- Espace membre pour les clients.

Design & brand: Moderne, accrocheur ("flash"), conçu pour la vente.
Intégrations & extras: Non spécifié.

en.dashboard:
Your admin dashboard is the control center for Optimaltvplus.

From the Admin area, you can manage the main parts of your site:
- Plans: add, update, or remove subscription offers
- Posts: manage articles or updates shown on the site
- Orders: review customer purchases
- Subscriptions: track active customer plans
- Channels: manage channel listings or service options
- Testimonials: add or edit customer reviews
- Contact submissions: read messages sent from the contact page
- Voice submissions: review requests or recordings sent through the voice assistant

To add or change content, open the Admin tab and choose the section you want. From there, you can create a new item, edit existing information, or delete anything you no longer want shown.

To change general site details, go to Settings in the Admin area. That’s where you can update things like business information, site text, and other overall options.

To check how the app is doing, open the dashboard home or Stats section. There you can view site activity, orders, and other business numbers in one place.

If you want to notify users, the best place to start is by updating plans, posts, or account-related information in the admin area so customers see the latest offers and updates. You can also review incoming customer activity there and respond based on orders or contact messages.

Your public site includes these main pages: Home, Plans, Firstaru, Omega, Features, Contact, Account, Checkout, Thank You, and Voice Assistant.
en.variables:
Great news! Your app is ready to go — no extra setup required.

Your site already includes the pages you asked for, including the new Firstaru and Omega pages with their pricing. It also comes with a checkout flow, contact form, member account area, thank-you page, and an admin space to manage the business side of things.

In short: you can start using it right away without connecting any outside services or adding any special keys.

fr.dashboard:
Le tableau de bord admin, c’est le centre de contrôle de votre site Optimaltvplus.

Dans l’espace Admin, vous pouvez gérer les sections principales du site :
- Forfaits : ajouter, modifier ou retirer des offres d’abonnement
- Articles : gérer les nouvelles, publications ou annonces
- Commandes : consulter les achats des clients
- Abonnements : suivre les forfaits actifs
- Chaînes : gérer les listes de chaînes ou options de service
- Témoignages : ajouter ou modifier les avis clients
- Soumissions de contact : lire les messages reçus depuis la page Contact
- Soumissions vocales : consulter les demandes envoyées par l’assistant vocal

Pour ajouter ou modifier du contenu, allez dans l’onglet Admin puis choisissez la section voulue. Vous pourrez ensuite créer un nouvel élément, corriger l’information existante ou supprimer ce qui ne doit plus apparaître.

Pour changer les réglages généraux du site, allez dans la section Paramètres de l’Admin. C’est là que vous pouvez ajuster les informations de votre entreprise, certains textes du site et les options générales.

Pour voir les résultats du site, ouvrez l’accueil du tableau de bord ou la section des statistiques. Vous pourrez y consulter l’activité du site, les commandes et d’autres chiffres utiles au même endroit.

Si vous voulez informer vos clients des nouveautés, le plus simple est de mettre à jour vos forfaits, vos articles ou les informations visibles dans l’espace client. Vous pouvez aussi suivre les nouvelles commandes et les messages reçus pour faire vos suivis.

Les pages visibles pour vos visiteurs incluent : Accueil, Forfaits, Firstaru, Omega, Fonctionnalités, Contact, Compte, Paiement, Remerciement et Assistant vocal.
fr.variables:
Bonne nouvelle! Votre application est prête à être utilisée — il n’y a aucun réglage supplémentaire à faire.

Votre site inclut déjà les pages demandées, y compris les nouvelles pages Firstaru et Omega avec leurs prix. Il comprend aussi un parcours d’achat, un formulaire de contact, un espace client, une page de remerciement et un espace d’administration pour gérer votre contenu.

Bref, vous pouvez commencer à l’utiliser tout de suite, sans connecter de services externes ni ajouter de clés spéciales.

promptHistory.changeNotes:
Initial generation of Optimal TV Plus, a bilingual (FR/EN) IPTV subscription PWA. Built with a dark, flashy green-accented design, a hero with 4 stat callouts, 4 subscription plans (Essentiel, Famille, Premium, Annuel), features grid, multi-device showcase, channel catalog, testimonials, blog. Implemented full end-to-end subscription flow: plan selection → login (built-in OTP via TenantSDK) → checkout → order creation → e-Transfer payment instructions → admin approves → subscription auto-activates with IPTV credentials visible in member area. Admin backend covers Plans, Orders (approving sets status=paid which auto-creates the subscription and sends a push notification), Subscriptions (M3U/Xtream credentials), Posts, Testimonials, Channels, Submissions. Server-side language switching via cookie+query. Hourly cron auto-expires subscriptions. Hero, devices, about, CTA, plans, posts all have AI-generated images.

Admin UX/UI enrichment: (1) Rebuilt admin-shell partial with polished modals, improved field rendering (labels prettified, bilingual hints, character counters for textareas, image preview always available, datetime/date/number with min/max enforcement), confirm-dialogs, success/error toasts, and proper empty states with CTA. (2) Dashboard now uses a richer stats grid with semantic color tokens, quick-action panel, recent orders & messages preview with status badges. (3) Admin sidebar polished with active state, mobile-friendly slide-over, footer links. (4) Improved admin-styles.css: toast system, modal animations, badge palette, accessible focus rings, larger touch targets, responsive table behavior, dark sidebar contrast. (5) Public CSS: stronger contrast on hero, fallback inline colors preserved on brand CTAs, improved card hover states. (6) Every module now has full CRUD UI via the shared shell (Add / Edit / Delete buttons wired to APIs, confirm before delete, toast feedback). (7) Functional content (plans, channels, testimonials, posts, orders, subscriptions) remains admin-manageable with all functional fields editable. (8) SEO metadata emitted as _seoMetadata for bilingual app.

promptHistory.prompt: Faire une autre onglet pour le serveur firstaru
promptHistory.changeNotes: Added a 'Firstaru' server tab to the account page credentials section. Subscribers now see two tabs — '🖥️ Serveur Principal' and '🌐 Serveur Firstaru' — each displaying that server's URL, username, and password with copy buttons. The admin Abonnements form now includes three new fields (firstaru_m3u_url, firstaru_credentials_username, firstaru_credentials_password) so the admin can assign Firstaru credentials per subscriber. A migrations.sql adds the new columns to the existing subscriptions table. No external API keys are required for this feature.

promptHistory.changeNotes:
Added two dedicated pricing pages: /firstaru (1m $30 / 3m $75 / 6m $140 / 12m $250 CAD) and /omega (1m $25 / 3m $60 / 6m $100 / 12m $200 CAD). Both pages are fully bilingual (FR/EN), display plan cards from the database using the existing checkout flow, and include a feature grid + CTA section. Plans are seeded into the plans table with name prefixes 'Firstaru' and 'Omega' so they're managed via the existing admin/plans module. The main /plans page and homepage are updated to filter out Firstaru/Omega plans (to avoid crowding the general catalogue). Navigation links to both pages added to the desktop nav, mobile menu, and footer quick links in both languages. No new database tables or admin views required — the existing Plans admin handles all plans.

Pre-flight smoke repair: Smoke repair: the home route (/) was timing out because it ran 4 sequential DB queries (plans, testimonials, channels, posts) on cold DB connections — all other routes hit 1–2 queries and passed fine. Fixed by converting the 4 sequential awaits to a single Promise.all, running all queries in parallel. This reduces worst-case response time from (sum of query latencies) to (max of query latencies) and prevents the cold-start timeout. No other logic changed.
